mainTopic: Does רבי יוסי accept that one prohibition can take effect on top of another when the new one is an איסור מוסיף (an expanded prohibition)? The case is two brothers married to two sisters, where one brother dies.
overview: Two brothers married two sisters, and one brother died. If the living brother is with the widow, she is both his אשת אח and his אחות אשה. רבי יוסי usually holds אין איסור חל על איסור, yet he says the man is liable for both. רבי אבהו explains that רבי יוסי agrees an איסור מוסיף, which forbids the woman to new people, does take effect. The גמרא shows this works only if the living brother married first. Forbidding more sisters to the same man is just an איסור כולל, not an איסור מוסיף. So רבא, backed by רבי יוחנן, explains it differently: the man is counted as sinning twice but punished only once, and the double count affects whether he is buried among the completely wicked. The גמרא then brings a related dispute between רבי חייא and בר קפרא in three cases: a זר serving on שבת, a בעל מום serving while טמא, and a זר eating מליקה. רבי חייא says a permission given in the מקדש covers only the proper people, so he is liable twice. בר קפרא says the permission is general, so he is liable once.

steps.title: רבי יוסי agrees that an expanded prohibition takes effect
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו states that even רבי יוסי, who normally holds אין איסור חל על איסור, agrees that a second prohibition takes effect if it is an איסור מוסיף.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: רבי יוסי agrees that an expanding prohibition does take effect.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו limits רבי יוסי's rule. A second prohibition can take effect on top of a first one if it widens the prohibition to new people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי's normal rule is that once something is forbidden, a second prohibition cannot take effect on it. רבי אבהו says there is an exception. If the new prohibition makes the item forbidden to additional people who were not forbidden before, it also takes effect for the person who was already forbidden. This means he could be liable for both prohibitions.

keyTerms.meaning: Agrees, admits (here: agrees to an exception to his usual rule)
An 'adding' prohibition, one that newly forbids additional people
A prohibition does not take effect where another already exists (רבי יוסי's general rule)

steps.whyThisMatters: The rest of the passage tests whether this exception really covers every version of the two-brothers, two-sisters case.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:

phrases.notes: Even רבי יוסי admits a second prohibition takes effect if it forbids the thing to more people than before.

steps.title: This works only if the living brother married first
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that רבי אבהו's idea works when the living brother married first. It then asks what is 'added' when the dead brother married first.
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well where the living brother married first and the dead brother married afterward. Since a new prohibition was added for all the brothers, it was added for the living brother too. But where the dead brother married first and the living brother married afterward, what added prohibition is there?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אבהו. His exception fits one order of marriages, but not the opposite order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose the living brother married first. His wife's sister, the woman who later becomes the widow, is already forbidden to him as an אחות אשה. When the other brother later marries her, she becomes an אשת אח and is newly forbidden to all the brothers, so the prohibition is מוסיף and it reaches him as well. Now suppose the dead brother married first. She was already an אשת אח to all the brothers. When the living brother then marries her sister, the אחות אשה prohibition applies only to him, so no new people are added.

keyTerms.meaning: It works out fine (opening a challenge: 'this case is fine, but...')
The living brother / the brother who died

steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אבהו's claim that איסור מוסיף explains how a second prohibition takes effect according to רבי יוסי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: When the dead brother married first, the later אחות אשה prohibition affects only the living brother. Nothing is added for anyone else, so the איסור מוסיף exception does not apply.

steps.title: A possible defense: he became forbidden to all the sisters
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests a possible answer. Once the living brother married, all the sisters became forbidden to him, so something was added for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you would say: since he became forbidden to all the sisters...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible way to save רבי אבהו's idea. It is setting this up so it can respond in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before the living brother married, only one sister was forbidden to him, as his brother's wife. After he married one sister, every sister became forbidden to him as an אחות אשה. The suggestion is that this widening should count as 'adding' a prohibition.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you would say: introduces a suggested answer, usually about to be rejected

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Perhaps widening the prohibition to all the sisters for the living brother counts as an איסור מוסיף.

steps.title: That is only an inclusive prohibition, not an expanding one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the defense. Forbidding more women to the same man is an איסור כולל, not an איסור מוסיף.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggested answer. Adding more forbidden sisters for the same man is a different kind of prohibition, not the 'adding' kind רבי אבהו talked about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An איסור מוסיף makes the woman forbidden to new people. An איסור כולל only widens what is forbidden to the same person, here more sisters for one man. רבי אבהו said רבי יוסי agrees only to איסור מוסיף, so the challenge from step 2 still stands.

keyTerms.meaning: An 'including' prohibition: it widens what is forbidden for the same person, not for more people
This

steps.whatToRemember: Two kinds of 'bigger' prohibitions: איסור מוסיף adds more people, and איסור כולל adds more forbidden things for the same person. רבי אבהו's exception for רבי יוסי covers only איסור מוסיף, so it cannot explain the case where the dead brother married first. Step 5 gives רבא's new approach, which solves this.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up כולל and מוסיף. Both make a prohibition 'bigger', but in different directions: more forbidden things for one person versus more people forbidden.

phrases.english: This is an inclusive prohibition.
phrases.notes: It widens what is forbidden for the same man, so it is not the 'adding' kind רבי אבהו meant.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the defense offered in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the suggested answer from step 3, so the challenge from step 2 against רבי אבהו stands. The גמרא then drops רבי אבהו's approach altogether ('אלא', step 5).
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The suggestion confuses איסור כולל (more forbidden women for the same man) with איסור מוסיף (the same woman forbidden to more people).

steps.title: רבא: Counted as two sins, punished for one
steps.stepSummary: רבא gives a new explanation of רבי יוסי: the man is considered to have sinned twice, but he is punished only once.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: I count him as if he did two sins, but he is only liable for one.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the איסור מוסיף answer fell apart in Step 4, רבא gives a brand-new way to understand רבי יוסי's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא no longer needs the second prohibition to legally take effect. רבי יוסי's 'liable for both' only means the man carries the guilt of two sins. In court he receives only one punishment, so the rule אין איסור חל על איסור still holds for punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals that the earlier approach is dropped.
I count it against him (I consider him as if...)
Liable to punishment

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבא means he gets two punishments. He is counted as having sinned twice, but בית דין punishes him only once.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
I ascribe to him
as though he transgressed twice,
yet he is liable for only one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the רבי אבהו approach, which Step 4 rejected
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the ruling (guilt versus punishment)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוסי's 'liable for both' meant that both prohibitions legally take effect, which needed an איסור מוסיף.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both sins count against him in moral terms, but he is punished only once.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן says the same thing
steps.stepSummary: When רבין came from ארץ ישראל, he reported that רבי יוחנן said the same as רבא.
steps.simpleTranslation: And likewise, when רבין came, he said that רבי יוחנן said: I count him as if he did two sins, but he is liable for only one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up רבא's explanation by showing that רבי יוחנן said the exact same words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is added to the idea itself. What changes is its strength: רבא's view now matches the tradition from ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: What difference does it make
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical result comes from counting him as having sinned twice if he is punished only once.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a quick clarifying question. If he gets only one punishment, why does it matter that he is counted as sinning twice?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets up the next step. The גמרא wants a real-world result, so that the 'two sins' idea is not just words.

steps.title: It decides where he is buried
steps.stepSummary: The difference is whether he is buried among the completely wicked.
steps.simpleTranslation: To bury him among the completely wicked.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the 'two sins' count matters for burial. It decides whether he is buried among the completely wicked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: People were buried next to others of a similar level. A person counted as having sinned twice is considered more wicked, and that affects where he is placed. So the double count has a real result even though the court punishes him only once.

keyTerms.meaning: To bury him

phrases.english: To bury him among the completely wicked.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The double count decides whether he is buried among the completely wicked.

steps.title: Dispute about a זר who served on שבת
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא connects the topic to a dispute. רבי חייא says a זר who did Temple service on שבת is liable twice, and בר קפרא says only once.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is the subject of a dispute, as it was stated: a זר who served on שבת. רבי חייא says he is liable for two. בר קפרא says he is liable for only one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a dispute between רבי חייא and בר קפרא about a similar question: does a person get punished for two prohibitions at once?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זר who did עבודה broke the ban on a זר serving, and he also did מלאכה on שבת. רבי חייא counts both prohibitions. בר קפרא counts only the זרות.

steps.title: Each one swears he heard it from רבי
steps.stepSummary: Each scholar swears that he heard his own view from רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא jumped up and swore: By the Temple service! This is what I heard from רבי: two. בר קפרא jumped up and swore: By the Temple service! This is what I heard from רבי: one.
steps.whatsHappening: Both scholars back up their positions by swearing that they received them from their teacher רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each one claims a tradition from the same teacher, so the two traditions cancel each other out. This prepares for the next steps, where each tries to prove his view with logic.

steps.title: רבי חייא's reasoning: שבת was permitted only for כהנים
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא argues that the permission to do מלאכה on שבת in the מקדש was given only to כהנים, so a זר breaks both זרות and שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא began to reason: שבת was forbidden to everyone. When it was permitted in the מקדש, it was permitted for כהנים. It was permitted for כהנים and not for זרים. So there is a sin here because of זרות, and there is a sin here because of שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the traditions conflict, רבי חייא now proves his view with logic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone was forbidden to do מלאכה on שבת. The מקדש exception was given only to כהנים, so for a זר the שבת prohibition stays fully in place. He therefore breaks two separate prohibitions.

steps.title: בר קפרא's reasoning: שבת was permitted in the מקדש
steps.stepSummary: בר קפרא argues that שבת was permitted in the מקדש in general, so the only sin is זרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר קפרא began to reason: שבת was forbidden to everyone. When it was permitted in the מקדש, it was permitted. So there is nothing here except זרות.
steps.whatsHappening: בר קפרא gives his own logical argument, which is the opposite of רבי חייא's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In his view, the permission for שבת in the מקדש is tied to the עבודה, not to who the person is. So שבת is not broken here at all. The only problem is that a זר did the service.

steps.title: רבי חייא's reasoning for the בעל מום who served while טמא
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא explains that the permission to serve while טמא was given only to unblemished כהנים, so a בעל מום who served while טמא breaks two prohibitions.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא began to reason: טומאה was forbidden to everyone. When it was permitted in the מקדש, it was permitted only for unblemished כהנים, and not for בעלי מומין. So this בעל מום sins twice: once for his blemish and once for טומאה.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא gives the reason behind his view from step 13: the blemished kohen who served while טמא is liable twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, serving while טמא is forbidden to everyone. In the cases where the תורה allows it, רבי חייא says the permission covers only כהנים who are fit to serve, meaning unblemished ones. A בעל מום never received that permission, so the טומאה prohibition still applies to him, on top of the prohibition of serving with a blemish.

steps.title: A third case: a זר who ate a מליקה offering
steps.stepSummary: The same two scholars argue about a זר who ate a מליקה offering. רבי חייא says he is liable twice and בר קפרא says once, and each swears he heard his view from רבי.
steps.simpleTranslation: A זר who ate a מליקה offering: רבי חייא says he is liable twice. בר קפרא says he is liable only once. רבי חייא jumped up and swore: 'By the Temple service! This is what I heard from רבי: two.' בר קפרא jumped up and swore: 'By the Temple service! This is what I heard from רבי: one.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third case where רבי חייא and בר קפרא argue in the same way, and again each swears he heard his opinion from רבי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bird killed by מליקה is not slaughtered, so outside the מקדש it would be forbidden to eat. Inside the מקדש the כהנים may eat it. A זר who eats it breaks the rule against a זר eating holy food, and the question is whether he also breaks the rule against eating an unslaughtered animal.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי חייא: a זר who ate מליקה is liable twice. בר קפרא: he is liable only once.

steps.title: רבי חייא's reasoning for the זר who ate the מליקה bird
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא explains that eating an unslaughtered bird was permitted in the מקדש only for כהנים, so a זר breaks both זרות and the rule against eating מליקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא began to reason: נבלה is forbidden to everyone. When it was permitted in the מקדש, it was permitted for כהנים. It was permitted for כהנים and not for זרים. So there is a sin here for זרות, and a sin here for eating a מליקה bird.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי חייא explains why the זר who ate מליקה is liable twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An unslaughtered animal (נבלה) is forbidden to all. The מקדש permission to eat a מליקה bird was given only to כהנים. A זר never got that permission, so for him the bird is still forbidden as unslaughtered meat, on top of the sin of a זר eating holy food.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal that died without proper שחיטה, which is forbidden to eat
The sin of a non-kohen doing or eating what is only for kohanim

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiya began to reason:
An unslaughtered animal was forbidden to everyone.
phrases.notes: A bird killed by מליקה wasn't slaughtered, so outside the מקדש it would count as נבלה.

phrases.english: When it was permitted in the Temple, it was permitted for kohanim.
It was permitted for kohanim, and not for non-kohanim.
So there is a sin here for being a non-kohen,
and there is a sin here for eating a pinched bird.

steps.raayaSupportSource: Logical argument: the permission to eat מליקה in the מקדש was given only to kohanim

steps.title: בר קפרא's reasoning for the זר who ate the מליקה bird
steps.stepSummary: בר קפרא explains that once the מליקה bird was permitted in the מקדש, it was permitted completely, so the זר is liable only for זרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: בר קפרא began to reason: נבלה is forbidden to everyone. When it was permitted in the מקדש, it was simply permitted. So the only sin here is זרות.
steps.whatsHappening: בר קפרא explains why the זר who ate מליקה is liable only once.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For בר קפרא, the מקדש permission removed the נבלה problem from the מליקה bird entirely. The bird is no longer forbidden meat. What remains is only that a זר ate food that belongs to כהנים.

keyTerms.meaning: To everyone
Was forbidden
Because of, on account of

steps.whatToRemember: In all three cases (שבת, טומאה, נבלה), the dispute is the same. רבי חייא says a permission given in the מקדש applies only to the proper people, so an improper person breaks two rules. בר קפרא says the permission is general, so only one rule is broken.

phrases.english: Bar Kappara began to reason:
An unslaughtered animal was forbidden to everyone;
when it was permitted in the Temple, it was permitted,
so there is a sin here only for being a non-kohen.
